title: Golden Knights hire Ryan Craig as coach, promoting him from AHL role
content:
The Vegas Golden Knights have hired Ryan Craig as head coach, the team announced on Wednesday. Craig had been the head coach of the Henderson Silver Knights, the Golden Knights’ AHL affiliate, since 2023.

Craig, 44, amassed a 96-95-13-12 record with the Silver Knights, leading them to their first playoff appearance since 2022 this past season, when they went 39-21-7-5. Before being named head coach of Henderson, he was an assistant coach with the Golden Knights for six seasons, winning the Stanley Cup with the team in 2023.

Craig also has a history with Vegas general manager Kelly McCrimmon, who owned and ran the Brandon Wheat Kings of the Western Hockey League when Craig played for the team.

A former forward, Craig played 198 NHL games and 711 AHL games over a pro career that spanned from 2003 to 2017, when he became an assistant for Vegas in its inaugural season. He scored 32 goals and 63 points in his NHL career, playing with the Tampa Bay Lightning, Pittsburgh Penguins and Columbus Blue Jackets.

Craig replaces John Tortorella, whose time as coach lasted only 79 days but included a division title, three playoff series victories and a Western Conference championship.

Craig’s hiring is a major departure for the Golden Knights. Their previous three full-time head coaches — Gerald Gallant, Pete DeBoer and Cassidy — each had at least two previous NHL head coaching stints before joining Vegas.

This hiring is very unlike the Golden Knights, but it’s also something they’ve been preparing for, for years. Craig may not have the experience of the other veteran coaches they’ve hired, but he knows the dressing room and the inner workings of the organization as well as anyone.

It’s rare for an assistant coach to survive one regime change, let alone three, and that’s what Craig did in Vegas. He coached as an assistant under Gallant, DeBoer and Cassidy before heading to Henderson to gain head coaching experience. He has worked with this group of players through several different coaching styles and understands their personalities and play as well as anyone.

McCrimmon has known Craig since Craig was a teenager. While this move has felt like it’s coming for quite a while, this is earlier than most would’ve expected Craig to take the helm in Vegas. The combination of unexpectedly firing Cassidy late in the season and the lack of obvious established coaching candidates on the market may have forced the Golden Knights’ hands a bit.

There’s plenty of reason for skepticism when it comes to handing the keys to a Stanley Cup contender to a first-time head coach, but Craig is well respected by the players and has several advantages over a typical rookie coach because of his path to this point.
